summary: The article describes how community colleges, led by Bright Horizons Community College (BHCC), have transformed adult education since the 2023-2024 academic year. Initiatives include Virtual Learning Hubs, a Mentorship for Success Initiative, flexible scheduling, business partnerships, and financial aid such as the $2 million Second Chance Scholarship Fund. Student and staff quotes illustrate how these programs help adults change careers and return to school.
one_line: Bright Horizons Community College expanded adult education with virtual hubs, mentorship, flexible schedules, business partnerships, and scholarships for returning learners.
key_facts: Bright Horizons Community College (BHCC) launched a series of adult learning initiatives on September 5, 2023, aimed at adults pivoting careers, gaining skills, or enriching their knowledge.
Dean Patricia Liu said BHCC's newly established Centers of Excellence focus on programs that are accessible, relevant, and transformative.
BHCC introduced 'Virtual Learning Hubs' on October 24, 2023, online platforms using virtual reality and advanced software to emulate a physical classroom.
In the Virtual Learning Hubs, adults can take part in a chemistry lab, a virtual book club, or public speaking practice in a simulated auditorium.
Dr. James Keller, director of technology integration at BHCC, said the Virtual Learning Hubs answer the needs of those limited by time or distance.
The 'Mentorship for Success Initiative' rolled out on November 15, 2023, matching each adult learner with a mentor in their field of study.
Janet Simmons, a 45-year-old healthcare management student, returned to school after 20 years and likened her mentor to a compass and personal cheerleader.

BHCC has offered flexible scheduling, including weekend intensives and night classes, since September 2023; Sarah Ahmed, a single mother of two studying business administration, relies on weekend classes.
Robert Gomez, a tradesman, moved from construction toward coding after a weekend bootcamp offered in the fall.
Business partnerships initiated in the winter of 2023 shaped curriculums around industry demands and often lead to internships; Dr. Rachel Mendez coordinates BHCC's business partnership program.
BHCC's 'Second Chance Scholarship Fund', introduced on January 4, 2024, allocated $2 million exclusively for adult learners.
The 'Dollars and Sense' financial literacy workshop series began in early September 2023 to help adults navigate funding their education.
